sn11.5:1.2: “Bhikkhus, once in the past the devas and the asuras were arrayed for battle.
sn11.5:1.3: Then Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, said to Sakka, lord of the devas:
sn11.5:1.4: ‘Lord of the devas, let there be victory by well-spoken counsel.’
sn11.5:1.5: And Sakka replied: ‘Vepacitti, let there be victory by well-spoken counsel.’
sn11.5:1.6: “Then, bhikkhus, the devas and the asuras appointed a panel of judges, saying:
sn11.5:1.7: ‘These will ascertain what has been well spoken and badly spoken by us.’
sn11.5:1.8: “Then Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, said to Sakka, lord of the devas:
sn11.5:1.9: ‘Speak a verse, lord of the devas.’
sn11.5:1.10: When this was said, Sakka said to Vepacitti:
sn11.5:1.11: ‘You, Vepacitti, being the senior deva here,
sn11.5:1.13: When this was said, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, recited this verse:
sn11.5:2.1: “‘Fools would vent their anger even more
sn11.5:2.2: If no one would keep them in check.
sn11.5:2.4: The wise man should restrain the fool.’
sn11.5:3.1: “When, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, spoke this verse, the asuras applauded but the devas were silent.
sn11.5:3.3: ‘Speak a verse, lord of the devas.’
sn11.5:3.4: When this was said, Sakka, lord of the devas, recited this verse:
sn11.5:4.2: Is the way to check the fool:
sn11.5:4.3: When one knows one’s foe is angry
sn11.5:5.1: “When, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, spoke this verse, the devas applauded but the asuras were silent.
sn11.5:5.4: When this was said, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, recited this verse:
sn11.5:6.3: When the fool thinks of you thus,
sn11.5:6.5: The dolt will chase you even more
sn11.5:6.6: As a bull does one who flees.’
sn11.5:7.1: “When, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, spoke this verse, the asuras applauded but the devas were silent.
sn11.5:7.3: ‘Speak a verse, lord of the devas.’
sn11.5:7.4: When this was said, Sakka, lord of the devas, recited these verses:
sn11.5:8.1: -891 “‘Let it be whether or not he thinks,
sn11.5:14.1: “When, bhikkhus, these verses were spoken by Sakka, lord of the devas, the devas applauded but the asuras were silent.
sn11.5:14.2: Then the panel of judges appointed by the devas and the asuras said this:
sn11.5:14.3: ‘The verses spoken by Vepacitti, lord of the asuras,
sn11.5:14.4: are in the sphere of punishment and violence; hence they entail conflict, contention, and strife.
sn11.5:14.5: But the verses spoken by Sakka, lord of the devas,
sn11.5:14.6: are in the sphere of nonpunishment and nonviolence; hence they entail freedom from conflict, freedom from contention, and freedom from strife.
sn11.5:14.7: Sakka, lord of the devas, has won the victory by well-spoken counsel.’
sn11.5:14.8: “In this way, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, won the victory by well-spoken counsel.”
